summary: Toothed wheels that transmit rotation at a fixed ratio, here involute spur gears whose profiles touch but never overlap.

variants.name: 1:1 spur pair with an axially sliding, slotted ignition gear
variants.applies_to: Wright 1903 spark-advance mechanism between the exhaust camshaft side and the ignition shaft
distinguishing_features: driven gear slides on a sleeve with a 45-degree slot
axial position set by a lever cam

dimensions.name: pressure angle
dimensions.basis: PRESSURE_ANGLE in scripts/gear_geometry.py; module, tooth counts and proportions there are teaching choices.

construction.note: Involute tooth outline from scripts/gear_geometry.py, derived
Involute tooth outline from scripts/gear_geometry.py, derived

function.role: Drive the ignition shaft from the exhaust-side shaft and change breaker phase by sliding along the slot.
function.motion: Both gears turn at the same speed; the ignition gear also moves axially under the advance lever, and the slot turns that movement into a phase shift.

envelope.statement: The pair touches but never overlaps through the mesh: minimum gap 0.078 mm against 0.02 mm required.
envelope.basis: interference-audit.json, gear_meshes, in the Wright revision-2 study.

intent.statement: Sliding the gear along the 45-degree slot advances or retards the ignition.

manufacturing.basis: The study records steel (part-spec.json) and states that the tooth flanks are illustrative (inventory 37).

recipe.note: Involute profile with backlash, solved mesh phase and a mesh-clearance check, shared by the accessory gears, the Wright ignition pair and the Langley trains. Declare meshes in scripts/accessory_gears.py (AGENTS.md); never type gear positions, rates or tooth phases into a builder.

instances.validation: Interference audit of the exported file is clean: 1,121 neighbouring pairs at rest, 133 poses of the baked clip, 0 overlaps (interference-audit.json); geometry is valid but historical accuracy is not verified (cad-validation.json).

gaps: Tooth counts and module of the pair are not recorded on this card; read them from cad_pipeline/wright_v2.py.

variants.name: Involute spur train with tooth counts solved to a documented ratio
variants.applies_to: Langley / Manly-Balzer cam reduction train (-1/4) and ignition train (0.5 and 2.5)
distinguishing_features: three external meshes reverse the cam direction
a coaxial small gear on the large gear
teeth read or solved to give exact ratios with no two gears of one plane overlapping

evidence.locator: p. 237 (cam at one quarter of crank speed, reversed)

dimensions.name: cam train teeth (pinion, large, small, idler, cam ring)
dimensions.basis: 24, 48, 18, 20 and 36 in cad_pipeline/langley_drive.py line 58 and inventory L25: chosen so the net ratio is exactly -1/4 with no overlap. Value is a list, so it is kept in the basis.

dimensions.name: cam train module
dimensions.basis: part-spec.json cam_train_module: layout and tooth counts are illustrative, read from a very crowded plate.

dimensions.name: sparker cam speed over crank speed
ignition train teeth (pinion, large gear, sparker cam)
dimensions.basis: 30, 60 and 12 give exactly 0.5 and 2.5 (part-spec.json ignition_gear_ratios rationale). Value is a list, so it is kept in the basis.

construction.note: Involute outline of each gear from scripts/gear_geometry.py, derived
Lightening pockets in the larger gears
Hub and axle where a gear is coaxial with another

function.role: Drive the ring cam at one quarter of crank speed in reverse, and drive the sparker cam and distributor from the crankshaft.
function.motion: Cam train: pinion to large gear, coaxial small gear to idler, idler to the cam-ring teeth. Ignition train: pinion to large gear to sparker cam.

envelope.statement: The three-mesh cam train reverses direction and reduces speed to exactly one quarter.
envelope.basis: Net ratio of the tooth counts in cad_pipeline/langley_drive.py; asserted by test_cam_turns_minus_a_quarter_through_three_meshes in scripts/test_langley_motion.py.

envelope.statement: All five meshes touch but never overlap: the smallest gap is 0.043 mm (sparker mesh) against 0.02 mm required.
envelope.basis: interference-audit.json, gear_meshes, in the Langley study.

intent.statement: A reversing train drives the cam opposite to the crank at one quarter of its speed.

manufacturing.basis: The study records steel (part-spec.json); the Memoir does not document the tooth form and the teeth are drawn as involute for geometric validity.

recipe.note: Involute profile with backlash, solved mesh phase and a mesh-clearance check, shared by the accessory gears, the Wright ignition pair and the Langley trains. Declare meshes in scripts/accessory_gears.py (AGENTS.md); never type gear positions, rates or tooth phases into a builder.

instances.validation: Interference audit of the exported file is clean: 1,492 neighbouring pairs at rest, 133 poses of the baked clip, 0 overlaps (interference-audit.json); mass check against the Memoir weight table in build-notes.md.

Interference audit of the exported file is clean: 1,492 neighbouring pairs at rest, 133 poses of the baked clip, 0 overlaps (interference-audit.json); mass check against the Memoir weight table in build-notes.md.

gaps: Tooth counts, module and tooth form are illustrative; the layout is interpreted from a very crowded plate.

cad-studies/langley-manly-balzer-1903/build-notes.md says the idler has 12 teeth, but cad_pipeline/langley_drive.py and inventory.json say 20; the idler cancels out of the net ratio, and this card follows the code.
